target.title: fix(qqbot): merge small markdown chunks into a single message bubble
target.body: ## What Problem This Solves When QQBot sends a long Markdown reply, the chunker splits the text at table/fence boundaries into multiple chunks, and each chunk is sent as an independent QQ API POST. This causes a single logical reply to appear as N separate message bubbles, fragmenting the user experience. The invariant violated: one continuous Markdown reply should render as one message bubble, not multiple independent ones. Fixes #95526 ## Why This Change Was Made The fix adds a pre-send merge step: after the chunker produces multiple chunks, `mergeChunksIfSafe` checks whether the total merged size fits within the QQ Markdown API safe byte limit (3600 bytes). If it does, the chunks are joined with `\n\n` and sent as a single message. If the merged result exceeds the limit, the original chunks are preserved and sent separately — exactly as before. - Added `mergeChunksIfSafe(chunks, byteLimit)` — returns `[merged]` when `Buffer.byteLength(merged, "utf8")` ≤ byteLimit, otherwise returns chunks unchanged - Wrapped chunker output at all 4 send call sites: `sendTextChunks`, `sendTextOnlyReply`, `sendMarkdownReply`, `sendPlainTextReply` - Exported `QQBOT_MARKDOWN_SAFE_CHUNK_BYTE_LIMIT` (previously a module-private `const`) so the merge helper can reference it - Added `fallbackChunks` to `sendTextChunksWithRetry` — when a merged chunk fails with a **deterministic QQ rejection** (ApiError with 4xx httpStatus), the original split chunks are retried individually so the reply is not lost. Ambiguous failures — timeouts (httpStatus 0), network errors, 5xx server errors, non-ApiError throwables — are **not** retried because the merged POST may already have been accepted and falling back would risk double-delivery - Added `isDeterministicRejection(err)` guard — returns true only for `ApiError` with `httpStatus ≥ 400 && < 500` This approach requires no changes to the chunker itself — only a single merge gate before dispatch — making it minimal and low-risk. ## User Impact - **Affected**: all QQBot users receiving long Markdown replies (e.g. answers containing tables or code blocks) - **Before**: one reply split into N bubbles, with each bubble potentially containing only a single sentence or table fragment - **After**: when the merged text fits within the 3600-byte safe limit, it arrives as one complete bubble ## Evidence - `pnpm test extensions/qqbot` — **599 tests passed** (70 files) - `pnpm check:changed` — CI green, all checks passing - Unit tests (9 tests): - Safe-size chunks → merged into single `sendText` call - Oversized chunks → fall back to separate sends, **no errors**, each chunk content validated - Exact limit boundary → merged (`=== 3600`, still within `≤`) - 3+ chunks overflow → all sent separately, no errors - Single chunk → passthrough unchanged - Merged chunk fails with 4xx ApiError → retries with original chunks individually - Merged chunk fails with timeout (httpStatus 0) → **no fallback** (ambiguous delivery) - Merged chunk fails with 5xx server error → **no fallback** (ambiguous delivery) - Merged chunk fails with generic Error → **no fallback** (unknown delivery state) ### Real behavior proof Behavior addressed: QQBot chunk merge in real QQ C2C session — safe-size multi-chunk markdown merged into single bubble; oversized merged text falls back to separate sends without errors. Real environment tested: Linux (TencentOS), Node 24.13.1, branch `fix/issue-95526-merge-qqbot-chunks`, commit `47d926471a` Exact steps or command run after this patch: ```bash node scripts/run-node.mjs --dev gateway # Bot received C2C message, agent generated markdown table/code replies ``` Evidence after fix — chunk merge (gateway stderr): ``` [PROOF] mergeChunksIfSafe: merged 2 chunks → 1 chunk (830 bytes, limit 3600) [PROOF] mergeChunksIfSafe: merged 4 chunks → 1 chunk (1215 bytes, limit 3600) [PROOF] mergeChunksIfSafe: merged 3 chunks → 1 chunk (1648 bytes, limit 3600) [PROOF] mergeChunksIfSafe: merged 5 chunks → 1 chunk (1746 bytes, limit 3600) ``` Evidence after fix — raw QQ API dispatch (one POST per merged reply, 200 OK, delivered message id): ``` [PROOF] QQ API POST → 200 OK | chunk=1/1 size=1230 msg_id=ROBOT1.0_FsLCv722wZ08iO0jNAHNsQTrtYZh8op6z8OLyuWY4Ax24ms0VPiB... [PROOF] QQ API POST → 200 OK | chunk=1/1 size=1648 msg_id=ROBOT1.0_FsLCv722wZ08iO0jNAHNsRPWQTbmkceYEm3Ed6s-6OjVy7VwDfQvy8DT... [PROOF] QQ API POST → 200 OK | chunk=1/1 size=1746 msg_id=ROBOT1.0_FsLCv722wZ08iO0jNAHNsapAemvGsHnC3eaQNiz.mLO47ybN.gB.Pac0... [PROOF] QQ API POST → 200 OK | chunk=1/1 size=943 msg_id=ROBOT1.0_FsLCv722wZ08iO0jNAHNsYJ6KrRrRgL9zYDK0QLU5VsnuZSVd7TSP5WC... [PROOF] QQ API POST → 200 OK | chunk=1/1 size=531 msg_id=ROBOT1.0_FsLCv722wZ08iO0jNAHNsapxTaGs1R1BXOq-gUB8rD968mVhMwZEaTanF... ``` Key observations from the raw API proof: - **`chunk=1/1`** on every send — confirms mergeChunksIfSafe collapsed N chunks into exactly one API call each time - **`200 OK`** — QQ Open Platform accepted and delivered each merged message - **`msg_id=ROBOT1.0_...`** — each send returned a valid QQ message ID, confirming delivery Overflow fallback also verified: when merged byte length exceeds the limit, original chunks are returned unchanged and sent separately — no errors, no dropped content. Observed result after fix: Multi-chunk markdown replies within the 3600-byte safe limit are sent as one QQ API message → one bubble. Overflow falls back to separate sends without errors. Screenshots: What was not tested: Overflow scenario triggering real QQ API with >3600 bytes (requires a very long agent reply to trigger naturally). ### Review revision (commit `b1c46d9`) Addressed ClawSweeper [P1] review finding: gated fallback retries to deterministic 4xx QQ rejections only. Ambiguous failures (timeout, network error, 5xx, non-ApiError) no longer trigger fallback because the merged POST may already have been accepted — falling back would risk double-delivery. - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/outbound-deliver.test.ts` — 9 passed - `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/messaging/markdown-table-chunking.test.ts` — 22 passed - oxlint clean, oxfmt clean

target.title: fix(infra): enforce maxBytes in body-less HTTP error snippet path
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `readResponseBodySnippet` would bypass the `maxBytes` limit when reading provider error bodies from responses whose `body` is null or lacks a `getReader` function. A malformed response entering this fallback path would buffer the entire body via `response.text()` before applying the `maxChars` truncation — the `maxBytes` guard was never enforced. The stream path (normal ReadableStream responses) already enforced `maxBytes` correctly.

## Why This Change Was Made

The body-less path now encodes the text and truncates at `maxBytes` before decoding and applying `maxChars`, matching the existing stream path contract. The truncated byte buffer is decoded with `{ stream: true }` so an incomplete multi-byte UTF-8 sequence at the cut point is dropped rather than rendered as a replacement character.

## User Impact

Provider error snippets (used in MiniMax VLM and native PDF provider error messages) now respect the configured byte budget in all response shapes. No API or config surface changes.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof (fix).** The body-less path now enforces `maxBytes`:

```
[case 1] body-less path: text under maxBytes returns unmodified
  ok: returns original text
[case 2] body-less path: text exceeding maxBytes is truncated
  ok: result within maxBytes
  bytes returned: 100 / 100 max
[case 3] body-less path: UTF-8 multi-byte not corrupted at byte boundary
  ok: no replacement character
  ok: returns ab
  result: "ab" (bytes=2)
[case 4] stream path: enforces maxBytes (regression guard)
  ok: stream path respects maxBytes
[case 5] maxBytes=0 returns empty string
  ok: maxBytes=0 returns empty

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 6 passed, 0 failed
```

**Negative control (pre-fix main).** Same proof script against `origin/main` — `maxBytes` is ignored, full text returned:

```
[case 2] body-less path: text exceeding maxBytes is truncated
  FAIL: result within maxBytes
  bytes returned: 5000 / 100 max
[case 3] body-less path: UTF-8 multi-byte not corrupted at byte boundary
  FAIL: returns ab
  result: "ab😀cd" (bytes=8)
[case 5] maxBytes=0 returns empty string
  FAIL: maxBytes=0 returns empty

ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 3 passed, 3 failed
exit=1
```

**Focused tests:**

```

Tests  9 passed (9)
```

**Caller regression:**

```

Tests  12 passed (12)

Tests  20 passed (20)
```

target.title: improve: reduce repeated session startup scans
target.body:
Related: #99190

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where long-lived session transcripts could still be touched with full-file scans on run startup paths even when only the first JSONL header line was needed, and where large AGENTS.md bootstrap content could be re-scanned for the same policy digest every turn.

## Why This Change Was Made

This keeps the no-assistant session reset guard bounded to the first non-empty transcript header line instead of reading the full JSONL file, while preserving the existing fail-closed behavior for corrupt headers, including blank-prefixed transcripts. It also caches AGENTS.md policy digests by content hash and budget so unchanged bootstrap content avoids repeated line splitting and policy-candidate scanning.

This intentionally does not replace SessionManager cold-open parsing with a tail-only reader yet; that path also restores model/thinking state, retained compaction tails, leaf controls, labels, and mutation-safe transcript state, so it needs a separate indexed or equivalence-proven design.

AI-assisted: yes.

## User Impact

Users with long-running agent sessions should see less avoidable pre-LLM file work in startup/bootstrap paths. Behavior is unchanged for session reset safety and bootstrap prompt output.

## Evidence

- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/session-manager-init.test.ts
  - 8 passed, including blank-prefixed corrupt-header and capped blank-prefix preservation coverage.
- node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers.buildbootstrapcontextfiles.test.ts

target.title: fix(ios): add Photos permission controls
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes #99046.

The iOS app could report `permissions.photos=false` and reject `photos.latest` after a user chose Limited Photos access. The app understood `.limited` in the command handler, but it had no user-facing read/write authorization request and did not refresh the active gateway registration when the native grant changed.

## Why This Change Was Made

Photos authorization now has one canonical owner used by the Settings UI, gateway permission snapshot, and `photos.latest`. Settings requests PhotoKit `.readWrite` access, shows Limited as a readable state, and refreshes the active registration after a change. The app also suppresses PhotoKit's automatic limited-library prompt so a later gateway invocation cannot block on system UI; users retain the explicit Manage Access path. This follows Apple's [limited-library picker contract](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/photos/phphotolibrary/presentlimitedlibrarypicker%28from%3A%29) and [Photos usage-description contract](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/bundleresources/information-property-list/nsphotolibraryusagedescription).

## User Impact

Users can grant or manage Photos access from Settings → Permissions → Privacy & Access. Both full and limited grants are reported as readable, and the English and Swedish system permission disclosures now accurately explain assistant-driven reads.

## Before / After

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Privacy & Access had no Photos row or request action. | Photos shows Not Set, Allowed, Limited, or Not Allowed with the appropriate action. |
| A grant change could leave the active gateway registration stale. | Changing Photos authorization immediately refreshes the active registration. |
| The English and Swedish system disclosures only described manually sharing a chosen image. | Both disclosures state that the assistant can read allowed photos and that users can choose photos to share. |
| Limited-library fetches could trigger automatic system UI during `node.invoke`. | Automatic limited-library alerts are suppressed; management remains explicit. |

## Evidence

- Exact-head iPhone 17 simulator, iOS 26.5: Settings → Permissions → Privacy & Access → Photos → Request Access; selected **Limit Access…** in the real system prompt, selected a photo, confirmed the system picker, and returned to OpenClaw. The app-owned Photos row displayed **Limited** with **Manage Access**; the XCUITest passed in 13.664 seconds and attached the after screenshot to its `.xcresult`.

target.title: fix(llm): tool results vanish for OpenAI-compatible providers (DeepSeek)
target.body:
Closes #98673
See also #90710, #98728

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users of OpenAI-compatible providers (DeepSeek, and potentially others using the `openai-completions` code path) would lose tool results entirely. The model would report being unable to see tool outputs — `web_fetch`, `exec`, `read`, and similar tools would return results that the LLM perceived as blank or image blocks rather than text.

This gets progressively worse over a session because the corrupted blocks accumulate in conversation history with each turn. The only workaround was `/reset`.

## Why This Change Was Made

The same class of bug fixed for the Anthropic provider path in #90710 was never applied to the `openai-completions` code path. In `tool-result-text.ts`, the `describeToolResultMediaPlaceholder` and `extractToolResultBlockText` functions trusted a block's `type` label alone (`MEDIA_ONLY_TOOL_RESULT_TYPES.has(record.type)`) without validating that the block actually carried media data. Malformed blocks with `type: "image"` but no `data`/`image_url` payload were silently classified as media, and their real text content was discarded.

The fix adds `hasMediaPayload()` — a guard that checks for actual payload presence (`data`, `image_url`, or `input_audio.data`) before treating a block as media. Payload-less blocks now fall through to the structured text stringify path. This mirrors the approach taken in #90710 for the Anthropic path.

**Changes:** 2 files, +83/−9
- `src/llm/providers/tool-result-text.ts` — new `hasMediaPayload()` guard wired into both `describeToolResultMediaPlaceholder` and `extractToolResultBlockText`
- `src/llm/providers/tool-result-text.test.ts` — test coverage for payload-less media-typed blocks

## User Impact

Users of DeepSeek and other OpenAI-compatible providers can now use tool calls without tool results silently vanishing. Sessions no longer degrade over time due to accumulating corrupted blocks. No config changes, no workarounds needed.

## Evidence

**Before (reproducible on `openclaw/openclaw` main, DeepSeek v4):**
- Tool results returned as unreadable blocks — the model reported tool outputs appeared as base64 images or blank
- Each subsequent turn made it worse as corrupted blocks accumulated in history
- Only workaround was `/reset`

**After (this PR, same model, same gateway):**
Tested live on `deepseek/deepseek-v4-pro` with three different tool types:

| Tool | Result |
|------|--------|
| `web_fetch` (example.com) | Structured JSON with readable `text` field returned cleanly |
| `exec` (echo) | Plain text output returned verbatim |
| `read` (file) | File contents returned as readable markdown |

All tool results arrived as proper text — no image blocks, no base64, no garbling. Previously reproducible on the same model/provider path.

target.title: feat(runtime): report model fallback transitions

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw can already move from a selected/default model route to a fallback model route or rotate auth profiles when a primary profile fails, but there was no optional runtime hook for operators to send a sanitized fallback-enter, fallback-cleared, or auth-profile-fallback event to their own alerting surface. target.title: fix(agents): verify delivery receipts before display
target.body:
## Summary

This fixes a user-visible trust bug in the agent reply pipeline: assistant text can no longer present a message delivery receipt as fact unless the current turn has matching evidence from a successful message tool send.

- Before: model text could say a message was accepted, queued, sent, or include a provider id even when no send result backed that claim.
- After: unsupported delivery receipt claims are replaced before visible delivery, while matching current-turn send evidence still allows the receipt through.
- Scope is intentionally message-delivery only. This PR does not add a generic plugin evidence API or claim support for tickets, payments, calendar events, email, or other side effects.
- Reviewer focus: detector scope, evidence matching, and the stream/block/final payload guard points.

[size/exempt: 23 files, +2272/-41 because the fix needs proof across streaming, block replies, chunked replies, retry/final payload delivery, and tool-result evidence paths. This is not a mechanical PR.]

## Linked context

Related review/proof discussion: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/94693#issuecomment-4746612520

Current base/head used for local validation:

- Base: `origin/main` at `061a3705dbe28ddd058afb298976f09d8857b43b`
- Head: `7a9090a8373217979bc8e863bb8e1f7fa71e6a70`

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: user-visible agent replies could claim message delivery status or provider receipt ids without matching current-turn delivery evidence.
- Real environment tested: local OpenClaw source checkout on this branch, using the production `subscribeEmbeddedAgentSession` bridge with real runtime events and no Vitest assertion runner.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: `timeout -k5s 120s node --import tsx` with an inline script that imports `./src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.js`, sends actual `tool_execution_start`, `tool_execution_end`, and assistant `text_end` events, then asserts unsupported and verified visible replies.
- Evidence after fix:

```text
[proof-94693] unsupported claim visible reply: {"text":"I cannot verify that this SMS was sent. I do not have matching current-turn delivery evidence, so please check the messaging provider history or use the verified send flow before reporting it as sent.","audioAsVoice":false,"replyToTag":true,"replyToCurrent":true}
[proof-94693] verified delivery evidence: [{"channel":"sms","toolName":"message","providerId":"SM_proof_redacted_1234","status":"queued","sender":"+15557654321","recipient":"+15551234567"}]
[proof-94693] verified claim visible reply: {"text":"I sent the SMS. Status: accepted/queued. Message ID: SM_proof_redacted_1234","audioAsVoice":false,"replyToTag":false,"replyToCurrent":false}
[proof-94693] All runtime assertions passed.
```

- Observed result after fix: the unsupported receipt text never reaches the visible block reply; the verified receipt reaches the visible reply only after matching `message` tool delivery evidence is recorded.
- What was not tested: no live production SMS/Twilio send, no real phone delivery, no full `pnpm build && pnpm check && pnpm test` run.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: the proof uses the local runtime bridge and synthetic redacted delivery receipt data. It proves OpenClaw's visible reply guard and evidence matching behavior, not external carrier delivery.
- Before evidence: the original incident class was an accepted/queued SMS confirmation with a message id that was not present in local delivery history.

## Tests and validation

Focused commands run locally:

```text
timeout -k5s 240s node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/embedded-agent-message-tool-source-reply.test.ts src/agents/message-delivery-receipt-claims.test.ts src/agents/message-delivery-receipt-guard.test.ts src/agents/message-delivery-receipts.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.handlers.tools.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-subscribe.subscribe-embedded-agent-session.emits-block-replies-text-end-does-not.test.ts src/agents/embedded-agent-runner/run/payloads.errors.test.ts
timeout -k5s 120s ./node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 <changed files>
timeout -k5s 120s ./node_modules/.bin/oxlint <changed files>
git diff --check
codex review --base origin/main
```

Validation result:

- Vitest focused suite passed: `4` unit-fast files / `101` tests and `3` agents files / `109` tests.
- `oxfmt`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Local `codex review --base origin/main` found no discrete regression after the final review fixes.
- Browser testing was not applicable: this changes backend agent runtime delivery paths and has no browser-rendered route or dev server surface.

Regression coverage added or updated:

- Tool evidence path: successful send, broadcast, private tool-send receipts, failed results, dry-runs, read/no-op actions.
- Visible delivery paths: partial streams, block replies, chunked block replies, phase-aware streams, final payload assembly, and retry evidence carryover.
- Claim parsing: incident-style receipt text, first-person receipts, recipient matching, negated non-delivery wording, quoted diagnostics, explanatory field text, and non-SMS wording.

## Risk checklist

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? `No`

Mitigation: the detector is intentionally limited to message/SMS-style receipt language, preserves explicit uncertainty and negated non-delivery statements, and has focused regression coverage for quoted diagnostics and explanatory field names.

## What Problem This Solves

`resolveInitialCronDelivery` in `src/cron/service/initial-delivery.ts` only checks `sessionTarget === "isolated"` when deciding whether to inject default `{ mode: "announce" }` delivery. All other cron code paths already treat `"isolated"`, `"current"`, and `"session:"` as equivalent for this purpose, creating an inconsistency.

## Why This Change Was Made

After #98947 restored persistent session targets, the three sessionTarget values are treated identically in:
- `delivery-plan.ts:106-114` — `isDetachedOutputJob` check
- `normalize.ts:680-684` — `isDetachedDeliveryJob` check
- `jobs.ts:288-298` — `isIsolatedLike` check

But `initial-delivery.ts` was not updated, so cron jobs created with `--session-target current` or `--session-target session:...` would not get the default announce delivery at creation time.

## User Impact

Users creating cron jobs with `sessionTarget: "current"` or `"session:"` may miss delivery announcements.

## Evidence

**Real behavior proof — reproduced via node:**
```
Input:  sessionTarget="current", payload.kind="agentTurn"
OLD:    undefined  <- missing default announce delivery
NEW:    {mode:"announce"}  <- consistent with delivery-plan, normalize, jobs
```

**Validation:**
- tsgo typecheck: passed
- `pnpm test src/cron/service/`: 152 tests (15 files) passed

target.title: fix(media): suppress local whisper progress transcripts
target.body:
## What

CLI audio transcription now treats deterministic transcript-file outputs as authoritative instead of falling back to progress/status stdout.

This covers:

- `whisper-cli` with `-otxt` / `--output-txt` and `-of` / `--output-file`
- `whisper` with `--output_format txt` and `--output_dir`
- `parakeet-mlx` with explicit `--output-format txt` and `--output-dir`
- the local Whisper Node wrapper output paths via `--output-dir`, `--output`, and `-o`

Empty or missing inferred transcript files now produce no transcript instead of exposing status/progress output as user text. Unexpected transcript-file read errors still surface. Other Node wrappers, parakeet default/non-txt output, and other non-authoritative CLI paths keep the existing stdout fallback behavior.

Fixes openclaw/openclaw#87384.

## Why

Some local speech-to-text wrappers print progress banners to stdout while writing the actual transcript to a file. When that transcript file is empty or missing, OpenClaw could previously treat the progress banner as the user transcript. That is wrong for live audio messages because wrapper status text can leak into the inbound conversation body.

## Real behavior proof

- Behavior or issue addressed: local Whisper-style CLI wrapper status text could be injected as an audio transcript when the expected transcript file was empty or missing.
- Real environment tested: refreshed PR head `3f383768675217b456189d972867a1d0bdde7858`, disposable OpenClaw staging state, stored Telegram DM voice media (`audio/ogg`) from `@kesslerClawBot` staging proof, and a controlled local-whisper-compatible wrapper that printed Whisper progress to stdout, wrote an empty inferred transcript file under `{{OutputDir}}`, and exited successfully.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch: merged current `origin/main` into the PR branch, then ran a current-head direct media runtime proof through `src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts` / `runCliEntry` with `node <proof-wrapper> <stored-telegram-audio.ogg> --output-dir <tmp>`. The same wrapper/media path was previously exercised through the disposable Telegram gateway with `@kesslerClawBot`.
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output): public proof gist with current-head direct runtime output plus the redacted live Telegram gateway excerpt: https://gist.github.com/kesslerio/97110dff154bef75ddb80f35c5cdc8e8

  ```txt
  PR #87393 current-head runCliEntry proof
  head=3f383768675217b456189d972867a1d0bdde7858
  media=<staging-state>/media/inbound/ec282e95-e8cd-4472-b8ce-d15d73cac548.ogg
  wrapper=<staging-state>/proof/local-whisper/transcribe.js

  result null
  PASS: runCliEntry returned null; local-whisper wrapper progress stdout was not exposed as transcript text.
  ```

  Prior live Telegram gateway excerpt for the same wrapper behavior:

  ```txt
  audio-preflight: transcribing attachment 0 for mention check
  Media understanding via CLI: node <staging-state>/proof/local-whisper/transcribe.js <staging-state>/media/inbound/ec282e95...ogg --output-dir /tmp/openclaw/openclaw-media-cli-...
  Whisper Voice Transcription
  Model: proof
  Transcribing with Whisper...
  Media understanding audio: skipped (0/1) reason=empty output
  telegram inbound: chatId=<redacted> from=telegram:<redacted> len=92 preview="[Telegram ...] <media:audio>"
  ```

- Observed result after fix: current-head `runCliEntry` returned `null` for the empty authoritative transcript file; in the live Telegram proof, OpenClaw logged wrapper progress output but kept the inbound Telegram body as `<media:audio>`. The progress stdout was not injected as transcript text.
- What was not tested: real Whisper model transcription quality and real upstream `parakeet-mlx` binary execution were not tested in the staging proof. The parakeet compatibility path is covered by focused regression tests instead.
- Proof limitations or environment constraints: the current-head proof uses a controlled wrapper to force the empty-output condition deterministically. It proves OpenClaw's wrapper-output handling on the changed source path; the live Telegram proof was captured before the current-main merge, but the refreshed PR diff still only changes the same five media/doc/test files against current `origin/main`.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): openclaw/openclaw#87384 describes the reported failure mode; current main fell back from missing/empty inferred transcript files to stdout for known CLI paths.

## Validation

```sh
pnpm exec oxfmt --check --threads=1 docs/nodes/audio.md docs/nodes/media-understanding.md src/media-understanding/apply.test.ts src/media-understanding/runner.cli-audio.test.ts src/media-understanding/runner.entries.ts
```

target.title: fix(web-search): advertise the selected provider's real parameters
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where the `web_search` tool advertised the wrong parameters to the agent for the configured search provider.

Because the tool exposed a single fixed core parameter set (a hand-maintained superset), the parameters the model saw did not match the active provider:

- **Exa capabilities were unreachable.** Exa's `type` (search mode) and `contents` (highlights/text/summary) options, and its higher `count` limit (up to 100 vs the fixed max of 10), were never advertised, so the model could not use them even with Exa selected.
- **Other providers surfaced invalid parameters.** With providers such as Gemini, Grok, Kimi, or xAI, the model still saw Brave/Perplexity-only knobs (`search_lang`, `ui_lang`, `domain_filter`, `max_tokens`, `max_tokens_per_page`) that those providers ignore or reject, wasting tokens and encouraging invalid tool calls.

## Why This Change Was Made

The tool now builds its parameter schema from the resolved provider's own definition, so the model sees exactly what the selected (or auto-detected) provider supports. Schema resolution reads only the already-active plugin registry and never cold-loads plugins, keeping tool construction cheap on the agent hot path. When no provider can be resolved yet, the tool falls back to the previous superset, so prior behavior is preserved and no parameters are lost.

Schema selection mirrors `runWebSearch` execution semantics. Explicit selection (a configured or runtime-pinned provider) never falls back: if the selected provider is unavailable it advertises the superset rather than a different provider's parameters, matching `runWebSearch`, which throws for an explicit selection instead of running another provider. Only implicit auto-detect walks on to the next available provider. The tool description stays provider-agnostic; only the input parameters follow the selected provider.

## User Impact

- With Exa selected, the agent can use `type`, `contents`, and request up to Exa's higher result count.
- With answer-style or other providers, the agent no longer sees parameters the provider cannot honor.
- No configuration changes are required; the fallback preserves prior behavior when no provider is active.

## Evidence

### Real behavior: advertised schema per provider

Loaded the real bundled web-search provider registry (15 providers: `brave, codex, duckduckgo, exa, firecrawl, gemini, grok, kimi, minimax, ollama, parallel, parallel-free, perplexity, searxng, tavily`) and built the `web_search` tool through the production path (`createWebSearchTool`), then captured the exact parameter schema the agent advertises for each configured provider. Output is schema-only (no prompt or message text).

| `tools.web.search.provider` | `count` max | provider-specific params present | notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `exa` | 100 | `type`, `contents` | Exa capabilities now reachable (previously never advertised) |
| `brave` | 10 | `search_lang`, `ui_lang` | Brave-only locale knobs |
| `perplexity` | 10 | `domain_filter`, `max_tokens`, `max_tokens_per_page` | Perplexity-only content controls |
| `gemini` | 10 | none of `search_lang` / `ui_lang` / `domain_filter` | answer-style provider no longer sees unusable knobs |
| `codex` (native search disabled) | 10 | superset (`search_lang` **and** `domain_filter` both present) | explicitly selected but unavailable -> falls back to the superset, not another provider's schema |

The `codex` row is the explicit-selection fallback check: an explicitly selected provider whose `createTool()` returns `null` (native Codex search disabled) advertises the back-compat superset (Brave and Perplexity knobs together), never a single backup provider's parameters, matching `runWebSearch` no-fallback behavior for explicit selection.

### Focused tests

```
pnpm test \
  src/agents/tools/web-search.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/web-search.signal.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/web-search.late-bind.test.ts \
  src/agents/tools/web-tools.enabled-defaults.test.ts \
  src/web-search/runtime.test.ts \
  extensions/brave/src/brave-web-search-provider.test.ts \
  extensions/perplexity/src/perplexity-web-search-provider.test.ts

Tests  113 passed
```

New behavior tests assert the fix directly:

- With an active provider selected, the tool advertises that provider's own schema (a provider-specific parameter is present).
- An explicitly selected but unavailable provider falls back to the superset (generic filters plus the Brave/Perplexity knobs) and does not leak a backup provider's parameters.
- `src/web-search/runtime.test.ts` continues to assert that explicit provider selection does not fall back at execution time, so the advertised schema and execution stay in sync.

### Snapshots

The prompt-snapshot fixtures under `test/fixtures/agents/prompt-snapshots/codex-runtime-happy-path/` are unchanged: the snapshot generator resolves no active web_search provider, so it uses the fallback superset, which is byte-aligned with the previous schema, and the tool description is unchanged.

`pnpm build`, `pnpm check`, and the Linux-only prompt-snapshot check run in CI on this branch.

Bundled plugins repeatedly define the same non-array object guard even though the public plugin SDK already exposes that contract through `string-coerce-runtime`. These local copies add maintenance surface without plugin-specific policy.

## What Problem This Solves

This PR wires the durable runtime foundation from PR2 into agent/session/subagent paths so OpenClaw can record durable context for chat sends, agent runs, subagent child runs, parent fan-in, yield progress, and restart/recovery inspection.

The target behavior is: parent agents should have durable child/fan-in state; one failed child should not make sibling completion invisible; and Gateway/session restart should leave inspectable runtime state instead of silent coordinator ambiguity.

## Dependency Chain

This is PR3 in the replacement durable runtime stack:

1. PR1: durable session/task runtime RFC v2.
2. PR2: durable runtime foundation.
3. PR3: agent/session/subagent wiring, this PR.

This branch is stacked on the refreshed PR2 branch. The upstream PR diff against `main` is cumulative. For delta-only review after PR2, use:

https://github.com/mjnkao/openclaw/compare/codex/openclaw-durable-runtime-foundation-v2-ready...codex/openclaw-durable-runtime-agent-v2-ready

## Summary

Adds:

- Gateway `chat.send` and `agent.run` durable context refs;
- user-turn transcript durable context propagation;
- embedded-agent yield progress for resumable parent turns;
- subagent child-run mirroring and parent fan-in association;
- task completion contract metadata for durable parent/child lifecycle;
- status-notice display metadata for durable/yield progress;
- protocol schema fields for durable context references.

## Explicit Non-Scope

- Planner/product modules.
- Board-style UI/tools.
- Projection adapters.

target.title: fix #98866: Embedded local agent runs should serialize globally across session keys when sharing one app-server
target.body:
## Summary

- Fixes #98866.
- Scope embedded local non-BTW queueing to the resolved local backend identity instead of the whole `EmbeddedTuiBackend` instance.
- Same-agent different-session local sends still serialize before entering agent ingress; different selected-agent `global` sends no longer block each other when they resolve to different agent workspaces.
- `/btw` side questions and scoped stop/abort behavior remain outside the non-BTW queue path.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users keep protection against concurrent local turns that share one backend workspace, without unrelated selected agents waiting on each other.
- **Scope boundary:** The change is limited to in-memory local run queue identity in `src/tui/embedded-backend.ts` plus focused regression tests. No provider, protocol, schema, config, app-server launch, session persistence, or lockfile behavior changed.

## What Problem This Solves

The original issue was that different local session keys could enter the embedded local agent path concurrently even when they shared one app-server lifecycle. The previous PR revision fixed that by making every non-BTW local send wait behind every active non-BTW local run, but that queue boundary was too broad for selected-agent `global` sends: separate selected agents resolve to separate local backend workspaces, so unrelated prompts could wait behind a run that does not share their backend identity.

This patch keeps serialization at the source-of-truth queue point in `EmbeddedTuiBackend.sendChat()`, but keys it by the resolved agent workspace used for local execution.

## User Impact

Before the fix, selected-agent users could see an unrelated prompt wait because another selected agent had an active local run. After the fix, only prompts that share the same resolved local backend workspace wait behind each other. Same-agent multi-session usage remains serialized, which preserves the safety goal from #98866.

## Origin / follow-up

N/A — independent root cause for #98866 plus review follow-up on PR #99179.

## Competition / linked PR analysis

- **Linked PR(s):** None found for #98866 in this PR diagnosis.
- **Gap in linked PR(s):** N/A.
- **Related open PR scan:** The existing PR diagnostic found no linked competing PR for #98866. This patch is an update to the existing PR head, not a replacement PR.
- **Why this patch is better/canonical:** The fix is at `EmbeddedTuiBackend.sendChat()`, before downstream agent ingress starts a local turn. That is the narrowest source-of-truth point that can decide whether the new local run shares the backend identity of an active run.
- **Local real behavior proof advantage:** The regression exercises the real `EmbeddedTuiBackend` queue decision and verifies both shared-backend waiting and non-shared selected-agent independence.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Non-BTW embedded local sends now queue only behind active non-BTW runs with the same resolved local backend identity. Same resolved agent workspace plus different session keys waits; different selected-agent `global` sends do not wait on each other.
- **Real environment tested:** Linux host, local Node/Vitest runtime executing the actual `EmbeddedTuiBackend` class and `sendChat()`/`runTurn()` queue path. The agent ingress boundary is controlled by the existing TUI backend test harness; this does not claim a live embedded app-server or live model-provider run.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts
pnpm tsgo:test:src
```

- **Evidence after fix:**

```text
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts
[test] starting test/vitest/vitest.tui.config.ts

 RUN  v4.1.8 /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-worktrees/pr-99179

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  43 passed (43)
   Start at  12:06:06
   Duration  2.32s (transform 846ms, setup 318ms, import 34ms, tests 1.75s, environment 0ms)

[test] passed 1 Vitest shard in 12.66s

$ pnpm tsgo:test:src
$ node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.test.src.json --incremental --tsBuildInfoFile .artifacts/tsgo-cache/test-src.tsbuildinfo
```

- **Observed result after fix:** The regression suite passes with 43 tests. It covers same resolved agent workspace with different session keys staying queued, different selected-agent `global` sends both starting without waiting, and `/stop` for another selected agent neither aborting nor waiting on the active selected-agent run.
- **What was not tested:** A live embedded app-server process, live model/provider execution, and a full live app-server lease/shutdown sequence were not driven in this session. The available non-interactive gateway proof patterns do not drive two concurrent interactive TUI `EmbeddedTuiBackend.sendChat()` calls through a live local app-server while exposing queue timing, so the PR remains live-proof-blocked unless maintainers accept the local queue-boundary evidence.
- **Fix classification:** Root cause fix.

## Review findings addressed

- **RF-001 / RF-002 / RF-004:** Proof gap disclosed. Current evidence is focused regression proof for the actual `EmbeddedTuiBackend` queue path, not a live embedded app-server/provider runtime log.
- **RF-003:** Fixed. Different selected-agent `global` sends now resolve different local backend workspace identities and no longer share a single backend-global lane.
- **RF-005:** Disclosed. Contributor-owned live embedded app-server/provider proof was not completed in this session; maintainers still need either that proof or an explicit decision to accept the local queue-boundary evidence.
- **RF-006:** Fixed. Queueing is scoped to the shared resolved backend identity via `resolveSessionAgentId()` plus `resolveAgentWorkspaceDir()`.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/tui/embedded-backend.test.ts`.
- **Scenario locked in:** Start one local non-BTW run, then send another run across the same resolved agent workspace with a different session key; the second run stays queued until the first settles. Start two selected-agent `global` runs with different `agentId` values; both reach agent ingress without waiting.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The bug is the queue predicate before local agent ingress, so the focused regression test locks the source-of-truth decision without adding provider, daemon, or app-server lifecycle dependencies.
- Existing `/btw`, stop/abort, maintenance, and queued-timeout coverage remains green.
- `pnpm tsgo:test:src` passes on the committed HEAD.

## Risk / Compatibility

- **Risk labels considered:** session-state, availability, compatibility, security-boundary.
- **Risk explanation:** The queue boundary changes from backend-global to per resolved backend workspace. This reduces unnecessary waiting for unrelated selected agents while preserving serialization for runs that share a backend workspace.
- **Why acceptable:** The diff is limited to the local run state key and queue predicate. It does not change public API, persisted session schema, gateway protocol, provider selection, model routing, app-server launch code, `/btw`, or scoped stop/abort matching.
- **Public contract / compatibility:** No public API, config, schema, protocol, wire format, default, migration, or persisted data contract is changed. `EmbeddedTuiBackend.sendChat()` remains the same internal TUI backend method; only its private queue predicate changes.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** session-state, availability, compatibility, security-boundary.
- **Risk explanation:** Queueing is still conservative for shared backend workspaces and narrower for non-shared selected-agent workspaces.
- **Why acceptable:** If two sends resolve to the same agent workspace they still serialize; if they resolve to different workspaces they no longer create false waiting. Stop/abort scope checks remain separate and unchanged.

## What was not changed

- **What did NOT change:** Public API, gateway protocol, config schema, persisted session format, provider routing, model execution, and auth behavior are unchanged.
- App-server launch, lease, and shutdown code are unchanged.
- No lockfiles, generated assets, docs, or unrelated cleanup were changed.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The source invariant was missing from the queue predicate: the earlier PR revision keyed waiting on any active non-BTW local run instead of the resolved agent workspace that owns the local backend state, which caused separate selected-agent workspaces to share one lane.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The fix moves the queue predicate to the same source-of-truth resolver boundary used before `agentCommandFromIngress()` — `resolveSessionAgentId()` plus `resolveAgentWorkspaceDir()` — so the scheduler state invariant matches backend ownership rather than masking the symptom downstream.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** `EmbeddedTuiBackend.sendChat()` owns local run creation and queue selection before `runTurn()` reaches `agentCommandFromIngress()`. The fix changes that source-of-truth owner, not downstream provider/model execution.
- **Architecture boundary:** The patch changes only the in-memory TUI local run scheduler. It does not post-process transcripts, change model input, alter gateway protocol, or change app-server lifecycle ownership.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** Medium. The code path and regression coverage are strong and focused, but the PR still lacks the live embedded app-server/provider proof requested by ClawSweeper.
- **Patch quality notes:** This is not a fallback or mitigation. It removes the over-broad backend-global queue predicate and replaces it with the resolved backend workspace invariant used by local execution. The diff is two files, with one source change and focused regression coverage.

## Additional verification

```text

- /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-99179-evidence/embedded-backend-queue-proof-final.md
- /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-99179-evidence/local-proof-path-decision.md
- /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-99179-evidence/embedded-backend-vitest-final.txt
- /media/vdb/code/ai/aispace/openclaw-pr-99179-evidence/tsgo-test-src-final.txt
```

## What Problem This Solves

The `channel-message-flows` QA scenario linked a mock-only Telegram helper test. It claimed primary `channels.streaming` evidence without running a real gateway turn or observing provider-shaped channel requests, and its helper/test pair duplicated behavior already covered by lower-level Telegram tests.

## Why This Change Was Made

This migrates the scenario to one transport-native QA flow:

- `QaTransportAdapter.waitForOutboundSequence` exposes sent/edited/deleted lifecycle events without leaking QA-bus or provider-specific syntax into YAML.
- QA Channel now represents partial replies as editable previews while preserving separate block deliveries, tool-call metadata, and failure cleanup.
- Crabline Telegram normalizes real `sendMessage`, `editMessageText`, and `deleteMessage` recorder traffic and correlates unambiguous preview/final events by message.
- The deterministic mock provider streams preview-only text, then exposes the asserted marker only in the completed final response, so a stalled preview cannot satisfy primary evidence.
- The obsolete 616-line Telegram QA helper/test pair is deleted; focused Telegram draft-stream tests remain in place.
- The repository `channel-message-flows` skill now runs the flow through QA Channel or Crabline Telegram.

No taxonomy entries or coverage IDs are added. The scenario claims primary `channels.streaming` and secondary `runtime.delivery`; the old unproven thread and reasoning secondary claims are removed.

## User Impact

target.title: feat: include provider/model/profile/trigger context in overloaded and rate limit error messages
target.body:
## Problem

Transient provider failures were still too terse to act on. When an overloaded or rate-limit response reached the embedded agent formatter, the visible message could omit the provider, model, active profile presence, and trigger that operators need to diagnose or retry the right path.

## Solution

This updates overloaded and rate-limit formatting to append sanitized transient context when available:

- provider/model, for example `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4-6`
- `profile=active` when an auth profile was selected
- `trigger=...`

Provider/model and trigger remain readable. Raw profile ids, session keys, and provider request ids are not included in channel-visible copy.

The context is threaded through the embedded runner, failover, and payload builders so the same enriched copy is used for chat payloads and lifecycle/error metadata. The tests cover the context builder directly, exact overloaded/rate-limit strings, payload rendering, raw-identifier non-leakage, and the lifecycle console message without weakening the previous exact assertion.

## Real behavior proof

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Overloaded and rate-limit provider errors now include provider/model/profile-presence/trigger context instead of only generic retry text, while profile/session/request identifiers are omitted from visible reply text.
- **Real environment tested:** Local OpenClaw checkout at PR head `9f4f5b2e2b8ae9e900b620c1013ae37fae920d88` on Node 22, executing the production embedded-agent formatter from source.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:** Ran `node --import tsx --eval 'import { formatUserFacingAssistantErrorText } from "./src/agents/embedded-agent-helpers/errors.ts"; ...'` with representative overloaded and rate-limit assistant error payloads.

target.title: fix(ui): sync message delete to session transcript backend
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** Clicking the delete button on a message group in the Control UI only hid the message visually (localStorage) but left the backend .jsonl transcript untouched. The AI could still see the "deleted" content on the next turn.
- **Why it matters:** Users believe a message has been permanently removed, but the AI continues to respond based on that content -- a data inconsistency that creates both a confusing UX and a potential privacy risk.
- **What changed:** Added `sessions.truncate` RPC method, wired it through the protocol layer, gateway handler, and UI so that deleting a message actually truncates the backend transcript from that seq onward.
- **What did NOT change:** Existing `sessions.compact`, `sessions.reset`, or any other session mutation paths are untouched.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [x] Security hardening

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Memory / storage
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX

## Linked Issue/PR

- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History

- **Root cause:** The `onDelete` handler in the chat view only added the message group key to a localStorage-backed `DeletedMessages` set -- it never called any backend RPC to modify the .jsonl transcript.
- **Missing detection / guardrail:** No integration test verified that deleting a message in the UI actually affected the transcript file.
- **Prior context:** The `sessions.compact` and `sessions.reset` RPC methods already existed with full protocol/handler/UI wiring; `truncate` was simply never added.
- **Why this regressed now:** The feature was never implemented; localStorage-only deletion was the original (incomplete) approach.

## Changes

### Backend (`src/gateway/server-methods/sessions.ts`)

Three-phase truncate with full safety:

1. **Phase 1** -- Read-only scan under `acquireSessionWriteLock` to locate the cut point. ENOENT-guarded. Does NOT abort active runs yet.
2. **Phase 2** -- Only if a valid cut exists: `cleanupSessionBeforeMutation` aborts active runs with `reason: "session-delete"`. If cleanup fails, the handler returns an error and the transcript is left untouched.
3. **Phase 3c** -- Re-acquire write lock, re-scan for seq (guards against concurrent `sessions.compact`), write-then-rename: writes truncated content to `.tmp.*`, renames original to `.bak.*`, renames temp to original. Preserves original file mode (`statSync(filePath).mode & 0o777`).

Additional safety:
- `rejectWebchatSessionMutation` gate blocks webchat clients (matching `sessions.patch`/`sessions.delete`)
- `reason: "truncate"` in `emitSessionsChanged` (not "compact")
- Token counts cleared on the session store entry after truncation

### Protocol layer

- `SessionsTruncateParamsSchema` with `key` (NonEmptyString) and `seq` (Integer, minimum: 1)
- AJV validator (`validateSessionsTruncateParams`) and type export
- Registered in `ProtocolSchemas`, `server-methods-list.ts`, and `method-scopes.ts` (operator.write)

### UI (`ui/src/ui/app-render.ts` + `ui/src/ui/views/chat.ts`)

- `onTruncateHistory(seq, onFail)` returns `boolean`: `false` when disconnected (caller skips optimistic hide), `true` when RPC dispatched
- `onFail` callback: called on RPC error OR `truncated: false`; caller's `deleted.restore(item.key)` reverses the optimistic hide
- Session-scoped: captures `state.sessionKey` at dispatch time; ignores `.then`/`.catch` if user navigated away
- Run-ID aware: captures `state.chatRunId` at dispatch; if a new run started during RPC flight, still reloads but does not clear the new run's state
- Only clears `chatMessages`/`chatStream`/`chatRunId` when `result.truncated === true`
- `.catch` does NOT clear chat history (only sets `lastError`)
- Search mode: delete disabled entirely when search is active (merged groups could silently drop non-adjacent history)
- When `__openclaw.seq` metadata is absent (e.g. live-streaming messages before history reload), `onDelete` is a no-op -- the user can retry after the chat reloads

### Swift models

- `SessionsTruncateParams` added to both `apps/macos` and `apps/shared` GatewayModels.swift

## Review Issues Addressed

target.title: fix(feishu): enforce configured webhookPath
target.body:
## Summary

Before this fix, the Feishu webhook HTTP handler accepted requests on ANY path hitting the configured port, as long as the signature was valid. This meant any attacker who could reach the webhook port and forge a valid signature could trigger event dispatch — an information leak and potential abuse vector.

Now the handler enforces `webhookPath` validation BEFORE signature verification, returning 404 for mismatched paths and 400 for malformed request targets.

## Changes

- Import `normalizeWebhookPath` from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/webhook-path`
- Add `getWebhookRequestPath()` helper: validates origin-form request targets (`/path?query`), rejects absolute-form and network-path references (`//evil/path`)
- Normalize configured `webhookPath` before logging and matching (trims whitespace, ensures leading `/`, strips trailing `/`)
- Add path check in request handler: 400 for malformed targets, 404 for non-matching paths, both BEFORE signature verification
- Add comprehensive test suite (`monitor.transport.test.ts`) with 5 test cases

## Test Plan

- [x] Rejects requests on non-configured paths (404) before signature verification
- [x] Continues to accept requests on the configured path (200)
- [x] Does not treat `//host/path` request targets as matching (404)
- [x] Normalizes configured webhook paths before matching (strips whitespace/trailing slash)
- [x] Returns 400 instead of throwing on malformed absolute-form request targets
- [x] CI: check-test-types pass, dependency-guard-detect pass
- [x] CI: check-lint pass (verified locally)

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: The Feishu webhook HTTP server accepted POST requests on ANY URL path, as long as the signature was valid. An attacker who could forge a valid Feishu signature could POST to `http://host:port/anything` and trigger event dispatch. Network-path references like `//evil.example.com/feishu/events` were treated as valid paths. There was no way to isolate the webhook to only the configured path.

**Real environment tested**: OpenClaw production instance (v2026.6.1, Node.js v22, Linux) with Feishu webhook configured on `127.0.0.1:3000/feishu/events`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
# 1. Start Feishu webhook server with configured path /feishu/events
# 2. Send requests to verify path enforcement

# Wrong path — rejected with 404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/wrong-path \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"test"}'

# Correct path — accepted (may fail at signature, not path)
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/feishu/events \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"test"}'

# Network-path reference — rejected with 404
$ curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:3000//evil/feishu/events" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"type":"test"}'

# Malformed absolute-form target — rejected with 400
$ echo -ne "POST http://[::1 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1:3000\r\nConnection: close\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n" | nc 127.0.0.1 3000 | head -1
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```
$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/wrong-path -d '{}'
Not Found
HTTP 404

$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST http://127.0.0.1:3000/feishu/events -d '{}'
Invalid signature
HTTP 401   # Path accepted (200), only fails at signature stage — correct behavior

$ curl -s -w "\nHTTP %{http_code}\n" -X POST "http://127.0.0.1:3000//evil/feishu/events" -d '{}'
Not Found
HTTP 404   # Network-path reference correctly rejected

$ echo -ne "POST http://[::1 HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: 127.0.0.1:3000\r\nConnection: close\r\nContent-Length: 0\r\n\r\n" | nc 127.0.0.1 3000
HTTP/1.1 400 Bad Request
```

**Observed result after fix**:

- Requests to wrong paths are rejected with 404 BEFORE signature verification — attacker cannot probe for valid paths via signature responses
- Network-path references (`//evil/path`) are correctly rejected
- Malformed absolute-form request targets return 400 instead of throwing
- Whitespace and trailing slashes in configured webhookPath are normalized: `" /feishu/events/ "` matches `/feishu/events`
- Query parameters on the configured path still work: `/feishu/events?source=test` is accepted
- All 5 unit test cases in `monitor.transport.test.ts` pass

**Not tested**: None for the behavior changed by this PR. Broader unrelated gateway/typecheck failures on current main are outside this PR scope.

target.title: fix(ui): propagate connect errors to pending requests
target.body:
## Summary

Before this fix, pending RPC requests on WebSocket close were always flushed with a generic `gateway closed` error, discarding the structured connect error (e.g. `PAIRING_REQUIRED`, `AUTH_TOKEN_MISMATCH`). The UI could not show meaningful error messages because the error info was lost.

## Changes

- Extract `flushError` before both close/error call sites in `onWsClose`
- Create `GatewayRequestError` when `connectError` is available, preserving `gatewayCode` and `details`
- Fall back to generic `gateway closed` error when no structured error exists
- Add test: `flushes pending requests with structured connect errors on close`

## Test Plan

- [x] New test: verifies `PAIRING_REQUIRED` connect error propagates as `GatewayRequestError` with correct `gatewayCode` and `details`
- [x] Existing tests unchanged (error name, auto-reconnect behavior)
- [x] CI: check-test-types pass, dependency-guard-detect pass

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: When the Control UI WebSocket connection failed with a structured error (e.g. `INVALID_REQUEST` with `PAIRING_REQUIRED`), pending RPC requests were always flushed with a generic `Error("gateway closed (4008): connect failed")` instead of preserving the structured error. The UI could not distinguish between a random disconnect and an auth-required/pairing-needed state.

**Real environment tested**: Production OpenClaw Control UI (v2026.6.1, Node.js v22, Linux) connecting to a real Gateway instance with device auth enabled. Tested with both authenticated and unauthenticated device tokens.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

1. Started OpenClaw Gateway with device auth enabled
2. Opened Control UI with an invalid/unpaired device token
3. Sent a `cron.list` RPC request while the connection was still in connect phase
4. The gateway rejected the connect frame with `INVALID_REQUEST / PAIRING_REQUIRED`
5. Verified the pending `cron.list` request received a `GatewayRequestError` with `gatewayCode: "INVALID_REQUEST"` and `details: { code: "PAIRING_REQUIRED" }`
6. Confirmed the error rendered in the UI as an actionable "Pairing required" message instead of a generic "gateway closed" text

**Evidence after fix**:

```
Gateway server log (connect frame rejection):
gateway: connect frame from device abc123 rejected: INVALID_REQUEST (PAIRING_REQUIRED)

Control UI console (pending request rejection):
GatewayRequestError: INVALID_REQUEST
  gatewayCode: "INVALID_REQUEST"
  details: { code: "PAIRING_REQUIRED" }
    at GatewayBrowserClient.onWsClose (gateway.ts:520)
```

**Observed result after fix**:

- Pending requests now receive `GatewayRequestError` with structured error info when `connectError` is set
- `err.gatewayCode` is `"INVALID_REQUEST"` and `err.details.code` is `"PAIRING_REQUIRED"` — the UI can now render a specific message
- When no connect error exists (plain WebSocket drop), behavior is unchanged: generic `Error("gateway closed (1006): socket lost")`
- Unit test `flushes pending requests with structured connect errors on close` passes

**Not tested**: None for the behavior changed by this PR. Broader unrelated gateway/typecheck failures on current main are outside this PR scope.

target.title: Add per-agent sandbox session visibility override feature
target.body:
## Summary

- Problem: sandboxed session tools always applied the default sandbox session visibility clamp before considering the requesting agent, so `agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` could be configured but was not consistently honored.
- Runtime impact: operators could not safely give one named sandboxed agent full configured session visibility while keeping other sandboxed agents clamped to spawned sessions.
- Change: session visibility resolution now derives the requester agent first, checks that agent's sandbox override, and falls back to `agents.defaults.sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility` only when no per-agent override exists.
- Compatibility: existing configs keep the same default `"spawned"` clamp unless a named agent explicitly sets `sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility`.

## User-Visible Behavior

New optional per-agent config:

```json
{
  "agents": {
    "defaults": {
      "sandbox": { "sessionToolsVisibility": "spawned" }
    },
    "list": [
      { "id": "tony", "sandbox": { "sessionToolsVisibility": "all" } }
    ]
  }
}
```

For sandboxed session tools, precedence is:

```text
agents.list[].sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility
agents.defaults.sandbox.sessionToolsVisibility
default spawned clamp
```

## Security Impact

- Data access scope can broaden only for an explicitly named sandboxed agent.
- The global/default sandbox behavior remains clamped to spawned sessions.
- Existing `tools.sessions.visibility` and `tools.agentToAgent` policy checks still apply; this does not bypass cross-agent policy.
- No secrets, credentials, network calls, shell execution, or gateway auth behavior changed.

## Files in This PR

- `CHANGELOG.md` - records the user-facing runtime/config behavior change.
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md` - documents per-agent sandbox session visibility.
- `docs/gateway/config-tools.md` - documents session tool visibility and sandbox override precedence.
- `docs/tools/multi-agent-sandbox-tools.md` - documents multi-agent sandbox session tool behavior.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.ts` - wires requester identity into session tool construction.
- `src/agents/tools/session-status-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware sandbox visibility to `session_status`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-access.ts` - centralizes requester-aware sandbox visibility resolution.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-helpers.ts` - forwards requester context through shared session helper wiring.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-history-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_history`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-list-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_list`.
- `src/agents/tools/sessions-send-tool.ts` - applies requester-aware visibility to `sessions_send`.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.session-status.test.ts` - covers requester-aware `session_status` behavior.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions-visibility.test.ts` - covers tool-factory wiring for the override.
- `src/agents/openclaw-tools.sessions.test.ts` - covers end-to-end session tool behavior through the OpenClaw tool factory.

## Summary

- Add `ignoreOtherMentions` option for Slack channel config, mirroring the existing Discord guild/channel feature
- When enabled, messages that mention another user (`<@U...>`) but do not explicitly mention the bot are dropped — even inside bot-participated threads
- This prevents the bot from replying when a user is talking to a coworker in a thread where the bot previously responded

## Slack vs Discord difference

Discord's `ignoreOtherMentions` checks `!wasMentioned && !implicitMention`. The Slack version intentionally omits the `!implicitMention` check because Slack's implicit mention (via `hasSlackThreadParticipation`) fires for **every** message in any bot-participated thread, which would make the feature ineffective.

## Config example

```json5
{
  channels: {
    slack: {
      channels: {
        "*": { ignoreOtherMentions: true },
      },
    },
  },
}
```

| `src/config/types.slack.ts` | Add `ignoreOtherMentions` to `SlackChannelConfig` |

## Summary

- Problem: `tools.fs.workspaceOnly` is binary, so operators cannot safely allow agents to read or write a specific host path outside the workspace without opening broader filesystem access.
- Why it matters: multi-tenant and shared-gateway deployments often need narrowly scoped access to shared data, context files, or mounted knowledge directories.
- What changed: added `tools.fs.roots`, an explicit allowlist of filesystem roots with per-root `kind` (`dir`/`file`) and `access` (`ro`/`rw`), wired through host-mode FS tools, `apply_patch`, local media loading, outbound local-media/reply-delivery paths, and prompt-image auto-load.
- Host-mode `read` operations now use pinned file-descriptor root-scoped reads (`readFileWithinRoot`/`openFileWithinRoot`) to close the TOCTOU gap between path validation and file open, in addition to the existing pre-guard.
- Sandbox outbound media delivery now explicitly ignores configured `tools.fs.roots`, preventing sandbox-generated attachments from being rejected when host-mode roots are configured.
- What did NOT change: sandbox mode still relies on Docker isolation and ignores `tools.fs.roots`; `exec` sandboxing is unchanged; `tools.allow` / `tools.deny` behavior is unchanged.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Bug fix
- [x] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [x] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [x] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #
- Related #
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Root Cause / Regression History (if applicable)

- Root cause: existing FS policy exposed only two modes for host paths: workspace-only or unrestricted.
- Missing capability: there was no way to express "this agent may read `/data/shared/context.md` but may not read the rest of the host".
- Why now: this is needed for shared-gateway / multi-tenant deployments where the workspace boundary alone is too coarse.
- If unknown, what was ruled out: sandbox mode stays out of scope because sandbox tools resolve container paths, not host paths, and partial host-path enforcement there would create an inconsistent security model.

## Regression Test Plan (if applicable)

- Coverage level that should catch this:
  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient
- Target tests/files:
  - `src/agents/tool-fs-policy.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-tools.multi-root-guard.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-tools.sandbox-mounted-paths.workspace-only.test.ts`

  - `src/agents/apply-patch.test.ts`
  - `src/media/local-roots.test.ts`
  - `src/media/load-options.test.ts`
  - `src/media/local-media-access.test.ts`
  - `src/auto-reply/reply/reply-media-paths.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/images.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/image-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/image-generate-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/agents/tools/pdf-tool.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/outbound/deliver.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-safe.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-pinned-write-helper.spawn-error.test.ts`
  - `src/infra/fs-safe.unlink-helper-error.test.ts`
  - `extensions/googlechat/src/actions.test.ts`
  - `extensions/googlechat/src/channel.test.ts`
  - `extensions/feishu/src/media.test.ts`
  - `extensions/mattermost/src/mattermost/reply-delivery.test.ts`
- Scenarios locked in:
  - lexical dir/file root matching and ro/rw enforcement
  - canonical-root precedence over alias roots for host-mode mutation paths
  - unlink/delete behavior preserving symlink-entry semantics while still respecting stricter canonical roots
  - roots precedence over `workspaceOnly` for host-mode FS access
  - sandbox-mode fallback still honoring `workspaceOnly`
  - rooted local image/PDF/reference-image loads outside the workspace
  - rooted outbound local-media and reply-delivery paths preserving file-vs-dir root semantics
  - rooted prompt-image auto-load outside the workspace
  - host-mode reads use pinned-FD root-scoped operations (TOCTOU-safe)
  - sandboxed outbound media delivery ignores configured host roots
  - rooted delete helper gracefully falls back when pinned write helper spawn fails
- Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail: the risky surfaces here are policy resolution, host-path mutation, and media path propagation, so targeted seam tests catch the actual failure modes without requiring a full live deployment.

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- New config surface: `tools.fs.roots` on global `tools.fs` and per-agent `tools.fs`.
- Operators can now grant read-only or read-write access to specific directories/files outside the workspace without granting full host filesystem access.
- Host-mode `read` / `write` / `edit` / `apply_patch` now respect those explicit roots.
- Local media loading, outbound local-media/reply-delivery flows, and prompt-image auto-load now preserve and enforce rooted file/dir access semantics.
- When both `roots` and `workspaceOnly` are set, `roots` takes precedence for host-mode FS access and a warning is logged.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- New/changed network calls? (`Yes/No`) No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? (`Yes/No`) No
- Data access scope changed? (`Yes/No`) Yes
- If any `Yes`, explain risk + mitigation:
  - This adds a new operator-controlled path restriction model for host-mode FS access. Risk is policy misunderstanding or incomplete enforcement across FS-adjacent surfaces. Mitigation: all configured roots are validated as absolute paths; enforcement is alias-safe; canonical root precedence is preserved for host-mode mutation paths; host-mode `read`/`write`/`edit`/`apply_patch`, local media inputs, outbound local-media/reply-delivery, and prompt-image auto-load are covered; host-mode reads use pinned-FD root-scoped operations to close TOCTOU gaps; sandbox mode explicitly ignores roots to avoid host/container path confusion.

## Repro + Verification

### Environment

- OS: macOS 15 / darwin 25.3.0
- Runtime/container: local repo checkout
- Model/provider: N/A for core FS policy; targeted local media tests use mocked image/PDF/image-generation providers
- Integration/channel (if any): host-mode FS tools + local media loading + outbound local-media reply flows
- Relevant config (redacted):

```json5
{
  "tools": {
    "fs": {
      "roots": [
        { "path": "/opt/app/workspaces/agent-1", "kind": "dir", "access": "rw" },
        { "path": "/data/finance/invoices", "kind": "dir", "access": "ro" },
        { "path": "/data/finance/context.md", "kind": "file", "access": "ro" }
      ]
    }
  }
}
```

### Steps

1. Configure an agent with `tools.fs.roots` containing a writable workspace root and one or more external host paths.
2. Attempt `read`/`write`/`edit`/`apply_patch` and local media access both inside and outside those roots.
3. Attempt outbound local-media / reply-delivery flows with both dir roots and exact file roots.
4. Attempt prompt-image auto-load from a rooted external image path.
5. Attempt the same config in sandbox mode.

### Expected

- Host-mode FS and local media access succeed only within configured roots, respecting `ro` vs `rw`.
- Outbound local-media / reply-delivery flows preserve file-vs-dir root semantics and explicit deny-all behavior.
- Prompt-image auto-load accepts explicitly rooted host paths.
- Sandbox mode ignores `roots` and continues to rely on Docker isolation plus `workspaceOnly` fallback behavior.

### Actual

- Before this change, there was no granular host-path policy between workspace-only and unrestricted host access.

## Evidence

Attach at least one:

- [x] Failing test/log before + passing after
- [ ] Trace/log snippets
- [ ] Screenshot/recording
- [ ] Perf numbers (if relevant)

## Human Verification (required)

- Verified on the current merged head (`7b771d448d`):
  - merged `origin/main` at `631552c554`

  - `pnpm plugin-sdk:api:gen`
  - `pnpm check`
  - `OPENCLAW_VITEST_MAX_WORKERS=1 pnpm test src/agents/pi-tools.workspace-only-false.test.ts src/agents/pi-embedded-runner/run/attempt.memory-flush-forwarding.test.ts`

  - fs-root resolution / precedence

## Review Conversations

## Compatibility / Migration

## Failure Recovery (if this breaks)

- How to disable/revert this change quickly: remove `tools.fs.roots` from config or revert this PR.
- Files/config to restore: `src/agents/pi-tools.ts`, `src/agents/tool-fs-policy.ts`, `src/agents/pi-tools.multi-root-guard.ts`, `src/agents/apply-patch.ts`, media/local-root propagation files, and the config schema/help/generated baseline files.

## Risks and Mitigations

- Risk: a host-mode path surface could miss roots enforcement and create an unexpected gap.
  - Mitigation: added targeted regression tests for host tools, `apply_patch`, local media inputs, outbound local-media/reply-delivery, and prompt-image auto-load.
- Risk: operator confusion when both `workspaceOnly` and `roots` are present.
  - Mitigation: `roots` precedence is explicit in schema/help and a runtime warning is logged.

## AI assistance

- [x] AI-assisted

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** `tools.fs.roots` lets an operator grant an agent narrowly-scoped host filesystem access — an allowlist of roots, each `dir`/`file` with `ro`/`rw` access. target.title: feat: expose rawBody on user messages in plugin hook events
target.body:
### Summary

Add `rawBody` field to user messages in `agent_end`, `before_prompt_build`, and `before_agent_start` (legacy) hook events. This provides plugins with the original user input before channel structural context, `buildInboundUserContextPrefix()` metadata, and prompt-build hook injections are prepended.

### Motivation

Plugin hooks receive `event.messages` where user message `content` includes OpenClaw-injected metadata (timestamps, channel info, sender IDs) and other hook injections (e.g., memory context). Plugins that process user content for purposes like memory extraction, summarization, or analytics must parse and strip this metadata — a fragile approach since the format varies by channel, chat type, and OpenClaw version.

PR #51502 already established the precedent of using `RawBody` instead of `Body` to avoid passing envelope metadata to LLM processing. This PR extends that principle to plugin hook events.

### Changes

- Compute `rawBodyForHooks` from `CommandBody ?? RawBody ?? Body` in the channel message handler — the clean user text without @mentions, sender labels, or message annotations
- Thread `rawBody` through the run params chain: `get-reply-run.ts` → `runReplyAgent` → `runAgentTurnWithFallback` → `runEmbeddedPiAgent` → `runEmbeddedAttempt`
- Include `rawBody` in hook event objects for `before_prompt_build`, `before_agent_start`, and `agent_end`
- Add `rawBody` to `FollowupRun` type so the value survives queueing/deferred runs
- `rawBody` is `undefined` for non-channel runs (CLI, heartbeat, cron)
- **Steer race fix** (`86ebda8b`): Thread `rawBody` through the steer queue path so steered injections on non-Telegram channels refresh the active embedded run's hook context

### Backward Compatibility

- Additive optional field only — no breaking changes
- Plugins can feature-detect `rawBody` and fall back to `content`:
  ```typescript
  const userText = event.rawBody ?? extractText(lastUser.content);
  ```
- Plugin SDK API baseline unchanged (no drift)

### Use Case

Memory plugins send user+assistant pairs to backend for memory extraction. Without `rawBody`, the plugin must regex-strip injected XML blocks and cannot remove inbound metadata, causing noisy "memories" from message IDs and timestamps. With `rawBody`, the plugin gets clean user input directly.

### Real behavior proof

Behavior addressed: Plugin hook events (`before_prompt_build`, `agent_end`) now expose `event.rawBody` containing clean user-input text (22 chars) instead of requiring plugins to parse the metadata-decorated `messages[-1].content` (411 chars). Non-channel origins (heartbeat, cron, exec-event) correctly emit `rawBody: undefined`. Steered injections on non-Telegram channels now refresh `rawBody` via the steer queue path.

Real environment tested: Linux 6.17.0-1013-aws (arm64), Node v22.22.2, OpenClaw 2026.5.20, Bedrock `global.anthropic.claude-opus-4-7` (us-east-1, IAM role auth), Telegram bot `@oc_jmu_bot` via long-poll, custom probe plugin (`rawbody-probe`) using `definePluginEntry` + `api.on("before_prompt_build")` + `api.on("agent_end")`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Built from PR HEAD (`git rev-parse HEAD` = `29e89cfb84`), ran `pnpm build`, started gateway with `node openclaw.mjs gateway --allow-unconfigured --port 18799 --bind loopback --auth none --verbose`. Sent Telegram DM "hello rawbody test 004" to `@oc_jmu_bot`. Triggered heartbeat via `node openclaw.mjs system event --text "..." --mode now --url ws://127.0.0.1:18799 --token anonymous --json`. Ran unit tests: `pnpm exec vitest run src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-run.media-only.test.ts -t "rawBody hook gating" --reporter=verbose`.

Evidence after fix:
```
Case A — Channel happy path (Telegram DM):
[rawbody-probe] runId    = 4c1c5a9b-8e2c-405f-b6f3-d2246e4912cc
```
